challenge.better_approach: Alternative: let clearance rule y admit a new proof whose PROVES names the ticket. That changes the outline 19.14.8.3 rule ('a ticket cannot call itself a fixit to get y'), which is Akien's, so no. Alternative: check at /sorted instead of cast. The sorted packet carries no bounds; the cast doc does, so the cast door is the earliest point that has the data. This is it.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That a proof file is recognisable from its path (a proofs/ segment and .py). A proof living elsewhere (skills/*/proofs/, bin/) still has a proofs/ segment; one with no proofs/ dir would slip past, which is the safe direction (a cast admitted, then refused at BUILDME as today). Also assumes latest_seal reads the seal the clearance reads, which both do from the code-relative root.
challenge.prior_art: Grepped CairnCommons tickets/ and questions/ for bug + new proof + cast door: no ticket does this. Near misses: c01503edd010 (PROVEME refuses a dead proof name) and 5f217a2d4bd6 (FIXME send-back). The fixes shape check in plan_shape.py resolves fixes paths against the cairn root and is the pattern to follow.
challenge.real_collision: None. Rule y at BUILDME still decides red-vs-green; this only refuses the case it can never admit (no seal at all). Outline 19.14.8 is unchanged.

answers.falsifier: A bug cast whose bounds.in names an unsealed proof is refused, the lack naming the proof and code-seam@v2, and nothing lands. The same doc as a code-seam casts. A bug whose bounds.in proofs are all sealed (or that names no proof) still casts. Wrong intent if a legitimate bug needs a new proof and its BUILDME can clear anyway, which q165/q166 measured it cannot.
answers.how: In cairn/tools/base/transitions.py cast_ticket, add one more lack. When node_class folds to bug, take each bounds.in path that sits under a proofs/ dir and ends .py. Resolve it against the cairn root, the same root clearance's CAIRN_ROOT and the fixes shape check use. Read its latest seal through cairn.tools.base.validation.latest_seal. A proof with no seal is a lack naming the path, why (a bug's BUILDME clears only onto a proof already sealed; rule y needs a real red), and the fix (cast it as code-seam@v2, rule x). A proof sealed red or green is not this check's business: rule y's red test stays at BUILDME. A red-first proof in cairn/tools/base/proofs casts into a scratch commons.
answers.traces_to: Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel): the same misclassification was re-derived twice (38dc3a0f93b1 at q165+q166, 2dda7060d84e caught before build), and each cost a re-cast. Law 4: the rule 'a bug brings no new proof' was policy, enforced only by a walk failing; this moves it to the earliest door.
answers.what: The cast door refuses a bug whose bounds.in names a proof that has never been sealed, and the refusal names code-seam@v2 as the class that admits a red-first proof.

bullets.text: A bug that brings a new proof is refused at cast, naming code-seam@v2, instead of at its BUILDME after a walk has started.
